Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-21 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maria Jensen (Redwood AE), Kunal Rao (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Alicia Park (Head of ML Ops), Derek Huang (CTO), Priya Menon (Security Lead), T. Rivera (Platform)

Summary (auto):
Quick renewal check-in to confirm Stratofleet's planned 20% capacity uplift, EU VPC onramp for data residency, and contract term extension. Agreement to run latency benchmarks and finalize pricing.

Topics: renewal pricing, EU VPC private deployment, latency targets, SOC2/KMS, rollout timeline, pilot scope

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maria Jensen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i know we're a little tight on time so we'll run through the renewal ask then dive into the eu vpc part.
[00:10] Alicia Park: thanks maria, appreciate it. quick context — we're planning to bump up production capacity about 20% starting q4 and want eu to be live for data residency, that's the big ask.
[00:25] Derek Huang: and timeline for the contract is end of july, so we'd like clarity on pricing adjustments and any infra lead times.
[00:34] Maria Jensen: got it. kunal, i'll hand the technical bits to you for the eu private onramp and latency expectations.
[00:39] Kunal Rao: yep hi all. couple clarifying q's — are you expecting Redwood Private (VPC) or a Dedicated VPC in our hosted environment? i know sometimes the terms blur.
[00:50] Tomás Rivera: we want a customer VPC with customer-managed keys, ideally in eu-west-1. on-prem is not required now but could be a future step. main thing is no egress to us-east.
[01:05] Kunal Rao: okay understood. we can do a private onramp in eu-west with customer KMS integration, and RBAC via your SAML IdP. there are a few things to lock down — network egress, firewall rules, and peak throughput at different seq lengths.
[01:20] Priya Menon: security items: rotation policy for KMS, audit log retention, and whether Redwood stores any persistent copies of payloads. also SOC 2 docs.
[01:30] Lena Ortiz: we have a SOC2 pack and a KMS integration guide — i'll add links after the call. on payload retention: by default host logs are redacted but we can set retention and PII redaction rules per account.
[01:45] Alicia Park: important — we need exact CLAs on retention for our legal team; they won't accept any copies outside eu region.
[01:53] Maria Jensen: understood, we'll make that explicit in the contract amendment.
[01:58] Derek Huang: curious about latency — our users are in europe; p95 should be under 220ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens). what can we expect with eu deployment vs routing to us?
[02:12] Kunal Rao: routing to eu will shave network hops. for comparable hardware, we generally see a 30-50ms improvement just from region proximity. however batching and KV caching behavior impacts p95 depending on concurrency. i can run your prompt set and get p50/p95/p99 numbers.
[02:28] Tomás Rivera: that would be great; we have a replay set and a synthetic spike harness.
[02:33] Kunal Rao: perfect — please share the sample prompts and we'll run a baseline. i'll include config: batch size, max tokens, quantization profile.
[02:40] Alicia Park: also, if we pick Dedicated vs Hosted, how does cost differ? we ran some math and dedicated looked cheaper per-token but incurs reserved commit.
[02:52] Maria Jensen: yes — Dedicated gives cost predictability and isolation. Hosted with EU routing is lower upfront but higher unit cost at scale. we'll send a side-by-side of unit economics for your expected Q4 usage.
[03:08] Derek Huang: obv reserved vs burst — we need burst headroom for peak flight booking windows. can Redwood handle burst across geoclusters?
[03:18] Kunal Rao: yes, we support burst across regions with smart routing. fallback policies can route to a compatible model variant in a neighboring region with explicit consent settings. we'll document SLOs for failover so your UX team knows expected p95 change.
[03:33] Priya Menon: on the fallback, what about data residency? if it falls back to us-east, that's unacceptable. need strict routing to eu-only.
[03:43] Kunal Rao: we can set policies: eu-strict route, and a secondary eu-compatible tier. if eu capacity exhausted, we can queue or return explicit 429s. that's configurable per environment.
[03:56] Maria Jensen: quick commercial note — contract amendment for EU VPC and extension to Jan 2028 will include additional fees for reserved capacity and longer term discount. i'll share a proposed amendment with line items.
[04:08] Derek Huang: can you itemize the pricing by token and by reserved GPU hour? legal wants transparency.
[04:16] Maria Jensen: yes we'll provide a spreadsheet that breaks down per-token, per-gpu reserved hour, and burst rates.
[04:22] Alicia Park: okay great. another thing: latency during long conversations with KV cache — we've seen regressions on other vendors where the cache thrashes. does Redwood have KV cache lock-in behavior?
[04:34] Kunal Rao: we use a KV cache system tuned for prefix reuse; there are heuristics to evict on low re-use. in practice we see better token cost with persistent KV and mitigated latency spikes. i can show you the caching telemetry in the console demo.
[04:48] Tomás Rivera: telemetry is key — our SREs want token-level drilldowns for cost allocation per route.
[04:55] Lena Ortiz: console has token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and audit logs. retention window can be extended as an add-on.
[05:05] Priya Menon: encryption at rest details? HSM or cloud-kms?
[05:09] Kunal Rao: both supported. for eu-sovereignty we'll recommend KMS in your cloud account with HW-backed keys if required. we integrate via KMIP or cloud-provider APIs.
[05:20] Alicia Park: rough ask — can we get an architecture sketch of eu VPC flow, key ownership, and where logs land? legal will need that.
[05:28] Maria Jensen: yes, tomás and priya we'll loop in the architecture diagram. expect docs in 1-2 business days.
[05:34] Derek Huang: about the renewal price — any flexibility for a 24-month extension vs 12-month? we prefer longer term if you can reduce unit cost.
[05:42] Maria Jensen: absolutely — longer commitments get stepped discounts. we can model 12/24/36 month tiers and the unit economics with and without burst.
[05:49] Kunal Rao: techn cal note — if you opt for a CPU fallback path for low-priority workloads we can save costs, but latency won't match GPU inference. good for background tasks. just flagging tradeoffs.
[06:02] Alicia Park: fair. our main production paths need GPU. background ingestion jobs can cpu. we'll outline which services.
[06:10] Derek Huang: any competitors we should be mindful of in your SSO/sovereignty stack? we've seen VertexAI pitch region-only endpoints.
[06:18] Maria Jensen: yes VertexAI and a smaller infra vendor CloudRunner have similar stories. our differentiation is unified runtime + explicit QoS controls and observable cost metrics.
[06:28] Alicia Park: ok, next step for us — legal + security will review the amendment and the SOC2 docs, SRE will want latency runs.
[06:35] Maria Jensen: to recap: we will send renewal quote + amendment, SOC2 + KMS design doc, and Kunal will run latency benchmarks once you share prompts. lena will send console links. anything else?
[06:46] Priya Menon: please include key rotation cadence options and a draft SLA for audit log retention.
[06:52] Lena Ortiz: noted, we'll include retention tiers.
[06:55] Tomás Rivera: i will share infra diagram and sample traffic replay by end of friday.
[07:00] Maria Jensen: great. scheduling — can we tentatively target a technical benchmark call week of 6/28?
[07:06] Derek Huang: works for me.
[07:08] Alicia Park: same.
[07:10] Maria Jensen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the benchmark.
[07:16] [meeting end]
